items.headline: Google ships DiffusionGemma, the first major open-weight text-diffusion model
items.diff_narrative: This storyline is net-new versus 2026-06-10, where the frontier-model thread was entirely Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 launch and its intent-routed safety architecture. Today shifts the open-model spotlight to Google's June 10 release of DiffusionGemma under Apache 2.0 - a 26B Mixture-of-Experts (3.8B active) on the Gemma 4 backbone that drops autoregressive decoding for text diffusion, refining 256-token blocks in parallel for up to 4x faster local inference, with a shipped Unsloth Sudoku fine-tune showcasing its bidirectional attention. Where 2026-06-10 framed the frontier as a closed, premium-priced, terms-enforced tier, today's lead is a permissively licensed local model that changes the decoding paradigm and the task profile of small on-device models. There is no precursor to diff against - it appears for the first time today.

items.headline: Agent tooling that pauses mid-run to ask the user - datasette-agent 0.2 ships ToolContext.ask_user
items.diff_narrative: A fresh agent-workflow thread with no counterpart on 2026-06-10, whose agent-stack coverage was the LiteLLM MCP command-injection flaw entering CISA's KEV catalog - a security/exposure angle. Today pivots to a capability angle: Simon Willison's June 10 datasette-agent 0.2a0 adds a ToolContext.ask_user primitive that suspends an agent run to ask the operator a yes/no, multiple-choice, or free-text question, with the paused conversation persisted to the database so it survives a server restart and resumes once answered, plus a save_query tool that stores agent-generated SQL only after explicit human approval. Versus yesterday's zero-trust, patch-the-proxy framing of the agent layer, today reframes the same layer around durable human-in-the-loop checkpoints as a first-class primitive. It is introduced today for the first time.

items.headline: Chip stocks snap back to open the week - Intel +8.5%, Micron +9% reversing the Broadcom washout
items.diff_narrative: This is the direct continuation and reversal of 2026-06-10's semiconductor item, which reported the Broadcom-triggered drawdown deepening - AMD off about 10% and Intel more than 8% in a single session on guidance contagion rather than any company-specific miss. Today updates that same selloff to its Monday June 8 snap-back: Intel up about 8.5% and Micron about 9% recovering from the prior Friday's roughly $1 trillion washout. The substantive change is not the price reversal but the leadership rotation and reframing - the rebound was led by US-manufacturing catalysts (reporting that Alphabet tapped Intel to make about 3 million in-house chips and that Nvidia is evaluating Intel's 18A process), rotating the story away from the merchant-GPU names that led the prior run toward domestic foundry capacity. Yesterday's read was that the cohort re-rates together on one hyperscaler-facing supplier's order book; today's is that the same AI-capex thesis is now being carried by a different mix of names centered on Intel as a potential merchant fab.

items.headline: AI events to plan around now - WWDC closes Friday, Databricks opens Monday, summer calendar firms up
items.diff_narrative: Carried forward from 2026-06-10's events bullet, still spanning the same three tracks (mainstream developer/data, AI-security, AI-chip/hardware) with date-passed entries dropped and still-upcoming ones held. The carry-forward additions are concrete firm-ups: AMD's Advancing AI 2026, listed yesterday only as slated for July, is now locked to July 22-23 at Moscone with MI400-series availability and a possible MI450 unveil expected; Hot Chips 2026 (Stanford, August 23-25) now shows early registration open through July 31; and the AI Engineer World's Fair detail gains a Harness Engineering keynote. The mainstream anchors advance by one day - WWDC26 now reaches its final day Friday June 12 rather than running through it - while the AI-security track (Confidential Computing Summit June 23-24, SecurityWeek AI Risk Summit August 11-12, Black Hat AI Summit August 4, DEF CON AI Village) and the standing Zenity global-expansion watch persist unchanged.
